report.source_text: fundoscopy showed bilateral parafoveolar microhemorrhages, and whitish lesions of the retina (Fig. 2A). Visual acuity was 0.3 (right eye) and 0.4 (left eye). Heidelberg spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) of the paramacular lesion revealed a hyperreflectivity at the junction of the outer plexiform layer and inner nuclear layer, revealing a focal ischemia (Fig. 3).

report.source_text: Progressive improvement of visual acuity and healing of vulvar ulcers were observed over the days following treatment initiation. Her estroprogestative pill was switched to a progestative-only pill owing to the risk of thrombosis associated with Behçet’s disease. The patient was discharged from hospital on day 4. Within 48 hours, a TNF blocking agent (intravenous infliximab 5 mg/kg/dose) was started. Visual acuity improved progressively. Infliximab was administered for a total of 4 months along with oral azathioprine up to 2 mg/kg/day. She will likely continue azathioprine for long-term maintenance, once corticosteroid tapering is completed. At the last visit, one and a half years after the initial symptoms, the patient had not experienced any relapse. At the last visit, Heidelberg SD-OCT (Fig. 3 right) showed atrophy of the macula. Besides, OCTA images remained unchanged, but the patient had recovered a vision of 1.0 (20/20) in both eyes.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A healthy 23-year-old woman initially presented with vulvar pain, edema, small vulvar lesions, and fever. Within one day, she developed bilateral blurred vision with suspected retinal hemorrhages, headache, lumbar pain, and persistent genital lesions. Ophthalmologic examination confirmed bilateral parafoveolar microhemorrhages, retinal whitish lesions, and retinal microangiopathy with ischemia on OCT. By day 4, genital lesions progressed to multiple painful deep ulcerations accompanied by dysuria and urinary retention. The patient was treated with intravenous pulsed methylprednisolone followed by systemic corticosteroids and later infliximab and azathioprine, resulting in progressive improvement and visual recovery at 1.5-year follow-up. No documentation of oral ulcers, joint symptoms, gastrointestinal symptoms, or laboratory/genetic test results (e.g., HLA-B51) was found. Immunopathological testing or biopsy results were not documented. The clinical course and response to immunosuppression support the diagnosis of Behçet’s disease.
